newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican conservatives defend private pension funds.
newsitem.headline: Mexican conservatives defend private pension funds.

text.p: Mexico's main conservative opposition party on Friday said a candidate in Mexico City's mayoral race was reckless in calling for workers to shun the country's new private pension system.

Cuauhtemoc Cardenas, the candidate of the left-wing Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD), told workers on Thursday they should boycott the new private pension funds, known as Afores. He said the commissions to be charged by the private funds were too high.

"He is inciting a legal breakaway, which could mean a severe financial blow to the country," National Action Party (PAN) Chairman Felipe Calderon told journalists. "I feel it was a wholly reckless and risky statement."
Mexico's ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party also defended the pension system, calling a news conference late Friday.
Some 10 million workers will have the option of choosing to invest in one of 18 Afores, which will begin operating on July 1. The Afores will manage an estimated $5.5 billion per year.
Funds belonging to workers who do not opt for a private Afore will be deposited with the central bank and managed by the state social security fund IMSS.
The Mexican government began the Afores program as part of a drive to bolster the country's low level of domestic savings, which it considers a sign of structural weakness in the economy.
Cardenas, who is the leading mayoral candidate, according to public opinion polls, said the Afores do not favor workers' interests.

"The Afores take over a part of the savings of the worker without giving benefits," the daily newspaper Reforma quoted Cardenas as saying. "And the so-called freedom of choice does not exist because eventually the worker is forced to join an Afore and pay a commission."
A source at the Afores managing body, known as the Consar, said it was not concerned that Cardenas' comments would hurt the pension system.
